articles.title: Jaylen Brown Talks 76ers' 'Growing Pains' After LeBron James Addition, 'Have A Lot to Get Better At'
articles.summary: Despite sitting atop the Eastern Conference with a 9-2 record to start the regular season, Jaylen Brown knows the Philadelphia 76ers still have room for improvement as they continue to figure out how this roster fits together.
articles.body:
Despite sitting atop the Eastern Conference with a 9-2 record to start the regular season, Jaylen Brown knows the Philadelphia 76ers still have room for improvement as they continue to figure out how this roster fits together.

Speaking to The Athletic's Tony Jones , Brown pushed back at the notion that there haven't been "growing pains" for the Sixers and they "have a lot to get better at" going forward:

"I mean, from our perspective, I think there have been some growing pains for sure. Even though we have been able to win, we still have a lot to get better at. We have a lot more to improve on. So the result? We're not so much fixated on the result. It's more so about the process. We have to improve our process and our mentality to create a winning environment. We've been winning games, but some of that stuff will catch up to you. So, you know, we have to nip it in the bud."

After all of the Sixers hype faded following their offseason trade for Brown and signing of LeBron James, there were questions about how a team built around four players who need the ball would make this work.

James did show his ability to take a backseat to a younger star last season when he took on the role of the No. 3 option for the Los Angeles Lakers since Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves were their top two players.

Perhaps the biggest surprise amid the the 76ers' strong start is they are a better defensive team than offensive at this point. They are sixth in defensive rating, compared to 20th in offensive rating.

The four-man lineup with Brown, James, Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey only has a 102.8 offensive rating in 111 minutes on the floor. Embiid, in particular, is off to a cold start with a 38.0 field-goal percentage in nine starts.

Another feather in Philadelphia's cap so far is its 8-0 record in clutch-time after Sunday's 127-121 win over the Chicago Bulls.

The fact that the 76ers have been this good already despite their stars not playing up to their full potential speaks well of how high their ceiling can be as long as everyone remains healthy.

Brown and the Sixers will look to keep their positive momentum going on Tuesday in a marquee matchup with the Boston Celtics at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

articles.title: Jordan Poole Gets Honest About Potential Future Warriors Reunion, 'It Just Feels Like Home'
articles.summary: Veteran guard Jordan Poole is open to a move back to the Bay Area should the opportunity to play for the Golden State Warriors materialize.
articles.body:
Veteran guard Jordan Poole is open to a move back to the Bay Area should the opportunity to play for the Golden State Warriors materialize.

Poole is a free agent following the 2026-27 season, so he could wind up back on the Warriors if the interest is there.

The New Orleans Pelicans reserve said that Golden State "just feels like home," and making the trek to Chase Center "definitely feels natural," per Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle .

"And I think it's pretty evident that the way I play is very fitting to how I used to play here," Poole said. "Nothing's changed, other than the systems that I'm in. We won a championship. So it works … to answer your question, definitely. This is my last year on the deal. I'm a free agent at the end of the season. So you never really know what's going to happen."

The Warriors selected Poole in the first round of the 2019 NBA draft, and he spent four years with the team. His trade to the Washington Wizards in July 2023 came less than a year after he had a physical altercation with teammate Draymond Green during a practice.

For his part, Green is equally amenable to having Poole back on the Warriors.

"I think he's an incredibly skilled player, and I'm an adult," he told the San Francisco Standard's Danny Emerman . "I don't carry issues. I've buried the hatchet with issues. So yeah, that's great. I know he loves the Bay Area. I can only imagine wanting to get back to the place that drafted you, the place where you had the most success. So yeah, that's amazing."

After being a full-time starter for the Wizards, Poole has shifted back to the bench with New Orleans. His usage this season has been more sporadic than ever. He's logging 19.6 minutes per night through five appearances.

The Warriors are on pace to have a lot of payroll flexibility next summer, but that will disappear fast as long as they continue to build around Stephen Curry and Green or a different star of similar significance.

When the time comes, Poole could be a good budget option to fill out the backcourt with the added benefit of his familiarity with Curry and Kerr's offense.

articles.title: LeBron James, Kevin Durant, Derrick Rose Among Investors in New Elite HS Basketball League
articles.summary: LeBron James and Kevin Durant are backing a new youth boys' basketball league expected to feature some of the sport's top prospects.
articles.body:
LeBron James and Kevin Durant are backing a new youth boys' basketball league expected to feature some of the sport's top prospects.

The two stars have joined the Orlando Magic's Paolo Banchero and Chicago Bulls icon Derrick Rose among investors in the Futures Basketball League (FBL), according to a Tuesday press release .

The FBL is set to feature 120 under-18 athletes across 12 teams during its inaugural 10-weekend season from April to August 2027.

Weekend tournaments will be "streamed or distributed on national television," according to FBL.

James is involved in this new venture alongside Maverick Carter through their investment firm LRMR Ventures, while Durant is associated with Rich Kleiman through Boardroom Sports Holdings.

The FBL said in its statement the league plans to provide a development path and NIL opportunities for players who were previously "spread across hundreds of teams and fragmented events."

The league stated players would be able to compete in FBL while still playing for high schools and participating in USA Basketball events, NCAA live periods or NBPA Top 100 Camp.

The FBL schedule potentially conflicts with the 2027 slate for the Nike EYBL, with which both James and Durant have been previously involved.

Youth players in FBL will be able to receive NIL compensation through cash or through equity in the league, although the FBL noted the equity proposal is "subject to administrative approvals."

High school NIL regulations are currently administrated by state athletic associations. Most states outside of Wyoming, Alabama, Mississippi and Hawaii allow active high school athletes to receive some form of NIL compensation, per the IMG Academy .

According to the FBL, prospects from the 2028 through 2031 classes have already started signing NIL contracts.

Some of these players will be announced in the upcoming weeks alongside other information including the FBL competition schedule, locations of team markets and more founding partners, according to the league.

articles.title: How Jayson Tatum and the Celtics haven't skipped a beat without Jaylen Brown
articles.summary: The Celtics enter Tuesday's heavyweight battle with Jaylen Brown's Sixers looking like the same elite squad they were last season.
articles.body:
Despite having Jayson Tatum for a grand total of 522 minutes during the 2025-26 regular season, the Boston Celtics won nearly 70% of their games, finished in the top five in the NBA in both offensive and defensive efficiency , and landed the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference. They reached that level of success thanks, in large part, to Tatum's longtime running mate, Jaylen Brown, turning in the finest individual season of his career en route to a sixth-place finish in MVP voting and an All-NBA Second Team selection.

After that, though, the Celtics traded Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers this summer — a move that you might have heard just a teensy bit about over the past five months, and that has been driving no small amount of conversation ahead of the first meeting of the season between Boston and Philly on Tuesday night.

Since that tectonic roster shift, as they seek to chart a new path forward with a shuffled-up rotation and without a franchise cornerstone, the Celtics have … won 80% of their games, rank in the top seven in the NBA in both offensive and defensive efficiency , and sit in the No. 2 seed in the Eastern Conference.

The more things change, the more they stay the same?

This, to some degree, was the bet that Brad Stevens made when he made the decision to move Brown for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks. In the longer term, exchanging Brown — who has three years and $185 million remaining on his contract, and is also in line for an extension — for George — who makes less this season , has a player option for next season and comes off the books one year earlier — tidies up the Celtics' balance sheet moving forward, potentially putting them in better position to remain competitive in the race for the top of the East several years down the line. (Say it with me, Brad: "optionality!" )

In the here-and-now, though, Stevens wagered that, as excellent as Brown was last season and as vital as he's been to the Celtics' perennial success for the past decade, the surrounding talent and head coach Joe Mazzulla's system would provide enough insulation to ensure that the team wouldn't skip too many beats without Brown. Through 10 games, at least? Boston looks pretty right about that.

The Celtics enter Tuesday's heavyweight battle with the Sixers looking broadly like the same elite squad they were last season. On offense, they sit in or near the top 10 in points scored and allowed per possession, and both team effective field goal percentage and opponents' eFG%. They're great at both avoiding turnovers and forcing them. They grab a ton of offensive rebounds and defend without fouling. They still jack a ton of 3s and make 'em at a top-10 clip, and still give up a ton of 3s in favor of protecting the rim without giving up the entire store on defense. They still play a methodical and effective brand of half-court basketball on offense; they're still great at preventing transition opportunities, despite sending multiple bodies to the offensive glass.

Even without Brown, the fundamentals of who the Celtics are haven't changed; the specifics of how they get there, though, are a little bit different. It starts with Tatum, now 18 months removed from rupturing his Achilles tendon and once again firmly entrenched as Boston's No. 1 option.

Tatum is still ironing out some of the wrinkles in his scoring game, finishing at substandard rates at the rim, from midrange and from beyond the 3-point arc. As he told reporters after blowing out the Charlotte Hornets last week, "I still got a little ways to to get back to being the best I ever felt."

Even with his bucket-getting lagging a bit, though, the 28-year-old is off to a flying start, averaging 27.1 points and 6 rebounds in 33.8 minutes per game. (He's been nails in crunch time, too, ranking eighth in the league in clutch scoring , with 21 points in 15 minutes on 8-for-13 shooting with 3 assists and 0 turnovers.) Just as Brown stepped into a higher-volume role in his absence last season, Tatum has slid into the monster void left by Brown's departure this season. He's finishing a career-high 33.3% of Boston's offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover, and leads the Celtics in usage, touches and time of possession .

As Gary Washburn of the Boston Globe put it , "Within the Celtics organization, there appears to be a sense of relief that the tension is gone" — that the team's hierarchy is clarified and established, with Tatum at the top of the pecking order, George comfortably slotting in behind him , and everybody else falling in line after that. Despite that, though, it hasn't felt like Tatum's got a stranglehold of Boston's offense — far from it, in fact.

Tatum's on-ball percentage — literally the share of his floor time that he has the ball in his hands — is down from where it was the past two seasons . His average time of possession of 5.1 minutes per game, 33rd in the NBA , between Donovan Mitchell and Ja Morant.

His willingness to get off the ball rather than pound it has helped produce a more egalitarian attack. Boston is averaging 27.2 assists per game, seventh-most in the NBA , up from 24.6 per game (27th) last season . Those dimes are leading to 70 points per game via assist, sixth-most in the league , up from 64 per game (22nd) last season .

Plenty of those helpers are coming directly off Tatum's fingertips. In the early going of the season, his playmaking has really leaped off the screen. Whether working in the pick-and-roll, operating out of the post, or surveying from the top of the floor at the nail, he's mapping the floor and delivering on-time and on-target feeds more often than ever. Tatum is averaging a career-high 7.8 assists against 2.8 turnovers per game, creating more baskets at the rim than all but five players in the NBA, according to PBP Stats , and setting up more 3-pointers than all but eight. He's one of just two players in the NBA in the top 10 in both scoring and assists. The other? The scorching-hot Luka Dončić .

The player Tatum has assisted the most thus far this season? George, who's been the recipient of 13 Tatum dimes , and who has looked like a hand-in-glove fit in his new digs.

George has picked up where he left off last season, when he came back from a 25-game suspension for violating the NBA/NBPA joint anti-drug program by taking "improper medication" for mental health issues to shine for the Sixers in their playoff push and their first-round victory over these same Celtics. He's averaging 20.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 30.1 minutes per game, shooting 50.7% on 2-pointers, 42.5% on 3-pointers while taking more than eight per game, and 80.8% from the free-throw line.

The nine-time All-Star isn't quite the full-tilt offensive force that he was earlier in his career, but he's fit in brilliantly as a secondary scorer and creator who can demand attention as an off-ball threat on offense, and a high-level, gap-filling playmaker who can help crank up the heat on the defensive end. He's still capable of assuming a larger role when called upon, too: When Tatum got the night off against the Bucks last Wednesday, George stepped to the forefront, scoring 25 points with 5 assists, 4 steals and 3 rebounds to lead the way in a 109-102 win .

"The way we're asking him to play is maybe a little bit different than what he's been asked to do in the past," Mazzulla told reporters in Milwaukee on Sunday. "He enjoys that, he's open-minded to it and he just works at it. He's very hard on himself. Holds himself to a very high standard, constantly watching film, taking notes in his journal and just processing the game. He takes pride in learning and getting better, and you're seeing the fruits of that."

The C's are also seeing the fruits of swapping Brown for George in the possession game. According to Jared Dubin's tracking at Last Night in Basketball , the Celtics finished 15th in the nightly possession battle last season, barely generating more scoring chances than their opposition on a night-to-night basis despite top-five finishes in both offensive rebounding rate and offensive turnover rate — due in large part to bottom-10 marks in both getting to the free-throw line and forcing turnovers on defense. Seven of the 14 teams that finished ahead of Boston last season won a playoff series — including all four conference finalists, and the Sixers team that eliminated them in the first round of the playoffs.

It is perhaps notable, then, that the rate at which the Celtics forced turnovers last season increased more with Brown off the floor than it did for any other player who logged at least 1,000 minutes — and that their forced turnover rate had been significantly higher with him off the floor in each of the previous two seasons.

So: Out went Brown, and in came George, a superior off-ball defender who has consistently posted higher steal rates, and center Mitchell Robinson, who'd built his reputation in New York as one of the league's premier extra-possession creators on offense and a disruptive presence in the middle on defense.

Robinson hasn't yet begun to make a major impact in tilting the math. After a sluggish start to the season following the Knicks' championship run and a short summer, the new arrival has started to round into shape, though, averaging 7 points, 8 rebounds and 2.7 steals-plus-blocks over the last three games , with the C's outscoring opponents by 30 points in his 53 minutes of floor time. All told, though, the Celtics have ratcheted up their board-crashing another notch, pulling in 34% of their missed shots through 10 games, up from 31.8% last season.

They're taking 6.5 more free-throw attempts per game, too, due in large part to a more concerted effort to pressure the rim. Last season, Boston ranked dead last in the share of its field goal attempts that came within four feet of the basket. This season, that's up to 17th .

Tatum's played a big role there. Replacing Brown's high-volume attacking as the only Celtic to rank in the top 50 in the league in drives to the basket per game, he's been living at the free-throw line. His previous career high in trips to the charity stripe was 8.4 per game, accumulated when averaging 36.9 minutes a night during the 2022-23 season. Through his first nine appearances of this season, he's taking 9.3 freebies in 33.8 minutes a night — a notable uptick on a per-minute and per-possession basis, and on pace for far and away the highest free-throw attempt rate of his career . (In fact, Tatum's .477 FTA rate ranks in the top 15 in the league among all non-centers .)

Most notably, though, the C's have been significantly more disruptive on the ball. Last season, Boston ranked 28th in the NBA in steals , 25th in deflections and 23rd in opponent turnover rate , playing more conservatively on defense in the belief that if they just stayed at home, funneled the ball to the areas and shooters they preferred, and contested, the math would work out in their favor over the long run.

This season, though — owing partly to the arrival of George, who's been a demon in the passing lanes in the early going — the Celtics are tied for 14th in steals , fifth in deflections and sixth in opponent turnover rate . They're cashing in on those miscues, too, scoring 20.8 points per game off turnovers — seventh-most in the league , and a full five points per game more than last season . (It's also on pace to be more than any Celtics team has posted since Rick Pitino was on the sidelines at the Garden, regaling reporters about Larry Bird and doors .)

Add up the gains in creating cough-ups, in getting to the line and in even more aggressively crashing the offensive boards, and the Celtics are now generating 4.1 more possessions per game than their opponents — the third-highest total in the league, according to Dubin's tracking .

Thanks to Tatum's playmaking, George's shotmaking and a collective effort from a deep rotation, the Celtics have made those extra possessions count, producing a top-five offense despite shooting just 63.2% at the rim as a team (a bottom-five mark ) and seeing multiple players (Tatum, Derrick White, Payton Pritchard, Baylor Scheierman, Jordan Walsh, Hugo González) struggle with frigid jumpers in the early going. If those perimeter players start to thaw out a little bit, this offense could hit a new level, and the Celtics could once again find themselves in the thick of the championship chase, even with Brown now plying his trade elsewhere in the division. The more things change, the more they stay the same.

articles.title: Luka Doncic's Exchange With Hawks Fans Shown in Trending Video After Lakers' Win
articles.summary: Nearly a decade on, trading Luka Dončić's draft rights continues to haunt the Atlanta Hawks.
articles.body:
Nearly a decade on, trading Luka Dončić's draft rights continues to haunt the Atlanta Hawks.

During the Los Angeles Lakers' 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday, Dončić exchanged trash talk with a group of fans along the sideline. He taunted that "you all wish you would have had me."

Atlanta famously picked Dončić with the No. 3 pick in the 2018 NBA draft but rerouted him to the Dallas Mavericks in a deal that included Trae Young.

The trade wasn't a complete disaster. Young was a four-time All-Star with the Hawks and helped get them to the Eastern Conference Finals in 2021.

But Dončić has proven to be the far bigger star, and Atlanta's future might've been very different if it had simply built around him.

articles.title: Celtics Hint at Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown Matchup With Hilarious Shootaround Song Before 76ers Game
articles.summary: The person in charge of the Boston Celtics' shootaround mix at Xfinity Mobile Arena ahead of Tuesday's game against the Philadelphia 76ers clearly has a sense of humor.
articles.body:
The person in charge of the Boston Celtics' shootaround mix at Xfinity Mobile Arena ahead of Tuesday's game against the Philadelphia 76ers clearly has a sense of humor.

Video from the Celtics' workout in Philly shows the song "Why Can't We Be Friends?" by the band War playing over the public address system.

The song could be interpreted in multiple ways, such as a plea for some semblance of harmony given the longstanding rivalry between the Celtics and 76ers.

But the most obvious reading is a joke about the relationship between Celtics star Jayson Tatum and former teammate/current Sixers forward Jaylen Brown.

Both players have downplayed any issues between them in the aftermath of Brown being traded to Philadelphia in the offseason. Brown famously said there's "no beef, but it might be little lamb chops and some gravy, you know what I mean?"

Tuesday night's matchup marks the first time Brown will be playing against his former team. Tipoff between the Celtics and Sixers is at 8 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard Injury, Return Timeline Updated by Raptors amid Reconditioning for Knee
articles.summary: Kawhi Leonard will sit out at least one more week with the knee injury that has sidelined him for all but two games of his first season back with the Toronto Raptors.
articles.body:
Kawhi Leonard will sit out at least one more week with the knee injury that has sidelined him for all but two games of his first season back with the Toronto Raptors.

Leonard "is continuing the reconditioning process after treatment to address left knee swelling" and will have his status updated in a week, the Raptors announced Tuesday.

Leonard last played Oct. 23 and has since missed eight games of the Raptors' 5-5 start to the season.

The Raptors said last week Leonard had completed treatment on his left knee and would now "begin the return to play process."

TSN's Josh Lewenberg reported Leonard has yet to progress to on-court work as of Tuesday.

The Raptors are playing four games against Eastern Conference opponents over the next week, starting with a back-to-back against the visiting Boston Celtics and host Philadelphia 76ers.

Toronto is then slated to face the defending champion New York Knicks twice, both at home, before Leonard's next update.

Leonard had averaged 19.5 points in 26 minutes per game over his first two contests with the Raptors.

Coach Darko Rajaković had previously indicated Leonard would slowly ramp up his workload as he continued adjusting from his late start to training camp stemming from his delayed trade from the Los Angeles Clippers.

Leonard's trade was approved in late September, about a month before the Raptors opened the season Oct. 21.

The Raptors announced ahead of the third game of the season on Oct. 25 Leonard would be a late scratch due to left knee swelling.

The team said two days later Leonard had undergone medical imaging that "revealed no acute injury" and would now begin treatment and rehabilitation while planning to be reevaluated in one week.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported the same day Leonard was expected to miss "a period of weeks."

The Raptors will hope Ja'Kobe Walter, who has averaged 11.6 points per game since replacing Leonard in the starting lineup, can contribute more consistent offensive production in the short term as Toronto looks to stay in contention to make it out of the East this spring.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown's Message to Celtics After Failed Bucks Trade Revealed in New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers wing Jaylen Brown was willing to stay with the Boston Celtics even after they attempted to trade him to the Milwaukee Bucks for Giannis Antetokounmpo, according to ESPN's Kris Rhim.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers wing Jaylen Brown was willing to stay with the Boston Celtics even after they attempted to trade him to the Milwaukee Bucks for Giannis Antetokounmpo, according to ESPN's Kris Rhim .

"Antetokounmpo got traded to the Miami Heat on June 22, and Brown was left wondering about his future in Bostonm" Rhim wrote. "He let the Celtics know that despite the failed trade he was willing to remain in Boston, but the team informed him he would be dealt anyway, the source told ESPN."

That report dropped Tuesday, the same day that Brown will face his former team for the first time this season. Brown played 10 years in Boston, making five All-Star teams and two All-NBA teams while winning two Eastern Conference titles and a championship.

Celtics' Shootaround Song Ahead of Tatum vs. Brown 🌶️

After the Bucks trade didn't work out, the Celtics soon dealt Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers for Paul George, two first-round draft picks and a pair of second-rounders.

Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens told reporters that the team essentially traded Brown due to concerns about how to best compete under the constraints of the current salary cap rules .

"The path looked a little bit more challenging to me," Stevens said. "I might be wrong. I'm not going to stand up there and be defensive about that. But the path looked a little bit more challenging with 70% of our (salary) cap, and such a high percent of our usage tied into two players."

Brown and Jayson Tatum were the two players in question. In the end, the Celtics dealt Brown to Philadelphia.

Brown is enjoying a great start with the 8-2 76ers, who lead the Eastern Conference. He's averaging 22.3 points on 47.7 percent shooting, 6.7 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game.

articles.title: Iyana Martín sale al rescate de España en Oviedo
articles.standfirst: Acaba con 18 puntos, 11 en el último cuarto y siete en los últimos cinco minutos para asegurar el triunfo ante la República Checa
articles.summary: Acaba con 18 puntos, 11 en el último cuarto y siete en los últimos cinco minutos para asegurar el triunfo ante la República Checa
articles.body: La selección femenina inició su camino al EuroBasket 2027 con una trabajada victoria sobre la República Checa en Oviedo, 73-71. No fue una victoria fácil, como indicaban los pronósticos, dada la diferencia que hay hoy en día entre los dos baloncestos, y tuvo que salir al rescate una Iyana Martín que no deja de sorprender, con cinco minutos fabulosos de magia al final. Gracias a ella, el equipo que entrena Miguel Méndez logró completar la primera de las tres misiones de estas Ventanas de clasificación en las que es muy peligroso fallar. Durante el partido dio la impresión de que cuando España aceleraba, cuando jugaba con ritmo y claridad, controlaba el partido y se marchaba en el marcador. Pero era una impresión que no duraba mucho y rápidamente las checas recuperaban puntos y volvían a comprimir el marcador. La prueba de esto fue el parcial de 11-0 entre el final del primer cuarto (20-11) y el principio del segundo con el que España estableció la máxima ventaja, 24-11, que parecía amenazar con romper el choque. En apenas dos minutos y medio, la República Checa volvía al partido (26-22). Poco después España volvió a estirarse, 31-24 y en poco tiempo las Checas volvieron de nuevo, 31-30, pero la selección de Méndez se fue al descanso con una más que interesante ventaja, 43-36. España se había sostenido con una enorme Raquel Carrera, la única jugadora interior superviviente del Mundial en acción, que firmaba 13 puntos y 4 rebotes. Y también con Iyana Martín, que recibió un homenaje en el descanso al jugar en su Oviedo natal, que al descanso estaba en 7 puntos y 4 asistencias. Las dos arrancaron bien el tercer cuarto para poner un 54-45 que volvía a despegar a las españolas, antes de que las checas volvieran a acercarse de forma peligrosa, 57-57, al final del acto. La República Checa aprovechaba un buen partido en el tiro, 7/13 en triples, para llevar algo de temor a las gradas llenas de aficionados españoles. España no estaba tirando bien (5/19 en triples), había perdido el control del ritmo y la batalla del rebote (26-34) y no aprovechaba las 20 asistencias que llevaba entonces. Las checas culminaron su remontada y se pusieron por delante, 59-64, ventaja que aumentó hasta un 61-67 con un triple de Sotolova a 6:46 para el final. El equipo checo, que llegó a Oviedo más bien para preparar sus duelos contra Bulgaria y Croacia, empezaba a creer en el milagro de ganar a la tercer potencia mundial. Fue Iyana la que despertó al equipo y al pabellón. Un triple suyo a 5:05 colocó el 66-67 y fue gasolina para el depósito de confianza desu equipo que estaba vacío. La selección empezó a defender con más intensidad espoleada por el público y tuvo una posesión para volver a estar arriba. Las checas acabaron con tanta euforia con dos acciones muy rápidas, 66-71 a 3:10. Otro triple de Iyana puso el 70-71 e inmediatamente después Araújo puso a la selección de nuevo por delante, 72-71. Un tiro libre más de la base abrochó el triunfo español con Iyana Martín (18 puntos) salvando a España de la derrota. 73 - España (20+23+14+16): Iyana Martín (18), Cazorla (4), Pueyo (6), Ginzo (7) y Carrera (13) -cinco inicial-, Etxarri (4), Ortiz (9), Ayuso (2), Torrens (3), Araújo (7), Vilaró (-) y Pendande (-). 71 - República Checa (11+25+21+14): Sotolova (12), Malikova (10), Vorackova (9), Pospisilova (10) y Stoupalova (-) -cinco inicial-, Zeithammerova (2), Fucikova (1), Holesinska (16), Svatonova (-), Kalna (7), Koucka (4) y Kytlicova (-). articles.title: Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum Reportedly Had 'Heart-to-Heart' Talk in France Before Celtics-76ers Trade
articles.summary: With the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics set to face each other for the first time this season on Tuesday, all eyes will be on the dynamic between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
With the Philadelphia 76ers and Boston Celtics set to face each other for the first time this season on Tuesday, all eyes will be on the dynamic between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown.

And they reportedly haven't spoken since a "heart-to-heart" conversation in France in late June.

"This was right after the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade to the Miami Heat where the Celtics offered Jaylen Brown but they missed out on it," ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday on NBA Today . "And this was also just days before Jaylen Brown's eventual trade to the 76ers. My understanding is Jaylen Brown confronted and approached Jayson Tatum at a dinner to discuss their future as a duo and where Jayson Tatum stood on all of it.

"It was described to me as a 'heart-to-heart' between these two sides that multiple people witnessed in person. But Jaylen Brown didn't leave that conversation knowing where his future was at moving forward."

Tatum and Brown played together in Boston for nine seasons and led the storied franchise to the championship during the 2023-24 campaign. They were one of the best duos in the league for much of their time together, although Brown took on more of a leading role last season when Tatum was sidelined by injury.

Brown also won the NBA Finals MVP and Eastern Conference Finals MVP during that championship run in 2024.

Their relationship has since taken center stage following the offseason trade that sent Brown to Philadelphia and brought Paul George back to Boston.

Last month, Tatum posted a video to his YouTube channel and said he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" regarding the Brown trade. However, Brown responded to that video with a cap emoji .

Tatum was also asked about the relationship and said he "called" and "texted" Brown the day he was traded.

He also said there was no "beef or ill will" and added, "This ain't no f--king Shaq and Kobe" and added, "At this point in our lives, we're too old to be having our relationship discussed X, Y, and Z like on the internet. If there's a conversation to be had, we can definitely have that."

For his part, Brown told reporters, "I saw that he said, 'It's no beef.' And I think he's right, there's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family, we've accomplished some great things, he's a hell of a basketball player and he's got a great PR team. It's no beef, but it might be little lamb chops and some gravy, you know what I mean? He should stay ready at all times."

He continued and said, "There's no beef, it should never ever be that. It's just basketball. We're both blessed. But it might be a little lamb chop. We'll be alright."

Tuesday is the first of four regular-season matchups between the two teams. It also wouldn't be surprising if they faced each other in the Eastern Conference playoffs seeing how they are both contenders.

And the relationship will surely be part of the story every time.

articles.title: Dear WNBA media, please stop telling fans to stick to basketball when the drama is what sells
articles.summary: Chiney Ogwumike asked the media to focus on the basketball, which makes the shooting numbers from Game 7 of the WNBA Finals an awkward place to start.
articles.body: During a recent episode of OutKick’s "Don’t @ Me with Dan Dakich," Dakich asked me, "What will be the biggest storyline in the WNBA this season, and will it have anything to do with basketball?" The second part was easy. No. ANGEL REESE’S WNBA FINALS SHOWED HOW CRITICISM OF HER PLAY BECOMES AN ACCUSATION OF RACISM And believe me, I care. I just spent over two weeks flying between San Francisco and Atlanta to cover the WNBA Finals. Who won was almost beside the point for me. I was there to ask why both teams were leaving the court before the national anthem and to hear what the players, coaches and the league had to say about it. In July, ESPN’s Chiney Ogwumike went on "First Take" and called for a reset in how the media covers Caitlin Clark and the WNBA. "In my opinion, we should be giving airtime to the beautiful basketball being played in the 30th year of the WNBA," she said. As for that beautiful basketball, are you sure that's where you want our attention? OK, let’s talk about the basketball Gabby Williams and Angel Reese entered Game 7 as co-favorites to win WNBA Finals MVP. Through six games, the two had combined to shoot 34.4% from the field. For context, the lowest field goal percentage ever recorded by an NBA Finals MVP was Kobe Bryant's 40.5% in 2010. At halftime of Game 7, Atlanta led 30–24. That’s 54 points on 31.8% shooting between the two teams. Reese and Williams combined for seven points on 3-for-8 shooting, with five from Reese and two from Williams. WHY ISN’T ANGEL REESE HELD TO THE CAITLIN CLARK STANDARD WHEN FANS ATTACK HER TEAMMATES? Then Williams scored 28 points in the second half as Golden State beat Atlanta 68–63 to win its first WNBA championship. She hit the go-ahead three with under three minutes left, finished with 30 points and four blocks, and deserved the trophy. She also shot 32.6% for the series, the lowest field goal percentage by a WNBA Finals MVP. Reese shot 40.5% from the field in the Finals, including 41.8% in the paint. She missed 28 of her 53 layups. She averaged nearly 13 rebounds, which is one reason you keep her on the floor. You’d still like your 6-foot-4 forward to make a few more shots around the basket. Is that the basketball that you want us to talk more about, WNBA media? Drama sells in the WNBA After Game 3, Reese taunted Golden State with the "too small" gesture, then smiled and waved as the Valkyries walked off the court. She’d just put up 21 points and 12 rebounds, Atlanta was up 2–1, and Reese claimed that she was getting inside the Valkyries’ heads. She proceeded to shoot 4-for-20 over the next two games and started complaining about the officiating. By Game 6, the player who’d called Golden State too small was one loss from going home. We’d seen this with Reese before. In the closing moments of the 2023 national championship game, Angel Reese followed Caitlin Clark around the court, taunting her with the "you can’t see me" gesture and pointing to her ring finger. A year later, 12.3 million people watched Clark's Iowa Hawkeyes eliminate Reese's LSU Tigers in the Elite Eight. This August, Clark’s Fever and Reese’s Dream drew 2.6 million viewers, ESPN’s biggest WNBA audience ever. Clark is the biggest draw in women’s basketball. Put Reese on the other side and you’ve got a rivalry people have been arguing about since they were in college. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD The WNBA reported 3.3 million viewers for Game 7. That’s a great number for the league (although it deserves the context that I provided in a recent column). If you tuned in to root against Angel Reese, you still got to watch Gabby Williams take over a championship game. If you want more people to watch, quit telling them what they’re supposed to care about.

articles.title: Kate Martin commits to Bendigo Spirit in WNBL
articles.summary: Former Hawkeye Kate Martin is going to continue her playing career in Australia.
articles.body:
Kate Martin's professional basketball journey is going to continue in a new part of the world.

It's been a whirlwind year for the former Iowa guard. She started the WNBA season with the Golden State Valkyries . She was waived in May and joined the Los Angeles Sparks . After spending over three months in LA, Martin was waived again. She proceeded to sign a developmental deal with the Chicago Sky, ultimately appearing in two games with the franchise.

Martin was set to play in Unrivaled, but the two sides came to a mutual contract termination before the season began. After stints with three WNBA teams and a snafu with Unrivaled, Martin now has a new home. She's set to join the Bendigo Spirit as a replacement player. The Spirit play in Australia's Women's National Basketball League (WNBL).

"I'm really excited to be joining the Bendigo Spirit and becoming part of such a successful program. I've heard great things about the WNBL and the standard of basketball in Australia, so I'm looking forward to challenging myself in a new environment.

"Bendigo has a really talented group and a strong team culture, and I'm excited to get to work, meet my teammates and hopefully contribute to another successful season," Martin said.

Martin's commitment to the club is pending league approval.

"Kate is a fantastic signing for our club and brings a wealth of experience from some of the best basketball environments in the world," Bendigo Spirit general manager Dan Jackson said of Martin.

"She's a tough competitor, a strong defender and a very capable outside shooter, but what really stands out is her basketball IQ, leadership and willingness to do whatever the team needs. She's played alongside some of the biggest names in the game and has built a reputation as an outstanding teammate, which is something we really value here at Bendigo."

The Spirit currently sit at the bottom of the WNBL standings with a 0-5 record. They'll hope Martin can bring a spark when she arrives.

Martin will be the second former Hawkeye to play in the WNBL recently. Last year, Lucy Olsen won a championship with the Townsville Fire. Martin and the Spirit will look to do the same as the season progresses. After a long year of constant changes, Martin will hope to find some stability in Australia.

articles.title: “Perfect Archetype”: Former College Player Weighs In on Estranged Valkyries Star’s Possible Future With Indiana Fever
articles.summary: Nobody wins a championship hoping to leave, and that is what makes the Golden State Valkyries’ offseason so strange. Less than two weeks after Game 7, and a...
articles.body:
Nobody wins a championship hoping to leave, and that is what makes the Golden State Valkyries' offseason so strange. Less than two weeks after Game 7, and a week after a parade along the Embarcadero, one member of the champions has been telling reporters back home that she may not return. Juste Jocyte was the first player the Valkyries ever drafted, and now fans are asking where she goes next. And according to one former college player, the Indiana Fever could be the stop she's looking for.

"If she's saying, 'I don't even know if I'd like to go back next year,' I'm pretty sure the Valkyries are not going to keep her," Rachel DeMita said on the Courtside Club Podcast in an Instagram clip.

"And with that, a lot of fans are speculating, like, where will she go? And the funny thing is, is, like, I actually think her game offensively could fit into literally any system. She's really tall…She moves so well. She cuts. She has a high IQ…Offensively, I feel like she could fit into any system. And even when you talk about the Fever, like, this is kind of the perfect archetype of the style of player that I've been talking about is kind of what they need," she added.

Jocyte was the No. 5 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft. Instead of playing right away, she stayed in Europe that season, then joined the Valkyries in May after finishing her EuroLeague season in Spain. She made her debut on May 25. But the minutes never came.

She played in 16 of the team's 44 games, averaging 3.1 points and 1.1 assists in about eight minutes a game, and she played just five minutes in two playoff games.

In an interview with Lithuania's BasketNews, she said, "I didn't really contribute much to that ring in terms of the game."

The bigger issue is her relationship with coach Natalie Nakase. Jocyte said the coaching staff gave her "a lot of excuses" for her role. A month into the season, Nakase reportedly made it clear Jocyte wouldn't play much, and she pointed to the team's wish for Jocyte to become a true point guard, learn the offense, and adjust to the physical game in the WNBA.

Jocyte said she never had a one-on-one talk with Nakase about her playing time. Valkyries beat writer Kenzo Fukuda also reported that Jocyte and her camp were frustrated that the reasons kept changing, which made it hard to know what she had to do to earn minutes.

She has also reportedly asked general manager Ohemaa Nyanin for a trade. She also said she is in no rush to return to the United States.

Valkyries owner Joe Lacob responded on Tim Kawakami's podcast. He said he understands why a competitive player who did not play would be upset. But he also said, "we'd really love to have her back." He said she is only 20 and should earn more playing time in the future.

Teams will see why. Jocyte became the youngest player to debut in the women's EuroLeague at age 14 and has been a two-time Lithuanian player of the year. She is under contract through 2028, with a team option for 2029, and will make less than $400,000 next season.

The Valkyries have a few options. Her contract is unprotected, so they could waive her at no cost, but that seems unlikely. They could trade her, though her comments have cut into their leverage. She could also sit out 2027.

Lithuania is hosting EuroBasket Women 2027 from June 16 to 27, and she was already set to miss part of the WNBA season to play in it. Or the two sides could patch things up, and she could return.

The clock is ticking, because this is the last offseason without an expansion draft until 2030. Cleveland joins in 2028, Detroit in 2029, and Philadelphia in 2030. The Valkyries would have to protect her ahead of better players or risk losing her for nothing.

That brings us back to the Indiana Fever. Indiana is looking for a new general manager after firing Amber Cox, and a hire is expected by December, ahead of January free agency. The next GM will have a tight cap. Aliyah Boston's supermax in 2027 takes up 20% of the cap, Caitlin Clark is eligible for a raise of up to 17%, and Kelsey Mitchell is a free agent.

Cheap, young talent will matter. The Sporting News also floated the Las Vegas Aces as a fit for a player who needs cheap shooting. No report says any team has contacted Jocyte, and the Indiana Fever have not been linked to her beyond DeMita's comments.

So the story of the champions' quietest player is only getting started. If DeMita is right, her next stop could say as much about the Indiana Fever's offseason as about hers.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown completely ignores Jayson Tatum's greeting before Celtics-76ers tip
articles.summary: As players took the court for opening tip, Tatum approached his former Celtics teammate, who’s now starting for the rival 76ers. Tatum made an effort to dap...
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown said prior to Tuesday's highly anticipated 76ers-Celtics game that he didn't intend to speak with Jayson Tatum .

At the opening tip, he was true to his word.

As players took the court before tipoff, Tatum approached his former Celtics teammate, who's now starring for the rival 76ers. Tatum made an effort to dap Brown up. Brown, who was busy spinning the basketball, acted like Tatum didn't exist.

Tatum then moved on to Brown's teammate, LeBron James, who was happy to share some pregame love with his rival before getting down to the business of basketball.

It was awkward to say the least and left Tatum standing at midcourt next to Brown like a man who'd just been left hanging.

The ball was then mercifully tipped to break the pregame tension.

When the game action started, it was Tatum who stuck the first blow. In their first one-on-one matchup of the game, Brown sized Tatum up from the wing beyond the 3-point arc. Tatum smothered him and poked the ball away off of Brown and out of bounds for a turnover.

Considering the chatter leading up to Tuesday's game, the pregame interaction went about as expected.

Tatum has downplayed any friction with his former All-NBA teammate.

"There's no animosity, there's no beef," Tatum said previously when asked about his relationship with Brown.

For Brown, who was vocal about his multitude of grievances before the Celtics traded in the offseason, there's clearly beef. Or lamb chops, as he prefers.

"There's no beef, but there might be a little lamb chops and gravy," Brown previously opined on his relationship with Tatum.

Brown doubled down on Sunday that he doesn't have anything to talk about with Tatum.

"It's nothing to talk about. I mean, he's on his side, I'm on my side," Brown said, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . "Just playing basketball. Both of us are trying to win, so nothing to talk about. Just check the ball up."

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith Criticizes Lakers’ Championship Hopes: ‘Never Seen A Team With Top 3 White Players Win A Ring’
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith believes the Lakers are not championship contenders just yet.
articles.body:
Stephen A. Smith's relationship with the Lakers had been strained over the years, partly because of LeBron James . But now that James is no longer with the Lakers, Smith still has serious concerns about how the Lakers' roster is built to contend for a championship around its new big three: Luka Doncic , Austin Reaves , and Walker Kessler .

The renowned sports analyst recently recorded an episode of his podcast, 'The Stephen A. Smith Show,' and spoke his mind on why he believes the Lakers are far from being championship contenders.

"Right now, Luka is on a roll. He's putting everybody on notice. He's going to be an MVP candidate. There's no doubt he's special," Stephen A. Smith clarified his feelings about Luka Doncic.

"But I've been on the record, and I ain't apologizing for it, by the way, because people thought I was stuttering. I guess I don't stutter that much. I said, 'I've never seen three players, led by three white guys spanning decades, ever lead an NBA team to a championship.'"

"I'm not backing down from that one bit. That's the route the Lakers have gone," Smith said initially on the show during his discussion with Jeff Teague.

"My opinion hasn't changed. We're 12 games into the season, and my opinion hasn't changed about the Los Angeles Lakers. I think the Lakers are a playoff team. I think they're going to get to the second round of the postseason, and then they're going to get humbled and go home."

"Western conference semifinal. That's what I think is going to happen with the Lakers… The way I look at it, I understand where you're coming from, no doubt."

"I would still look at Oklahoma City as being better. I would look at San Antonio as being better. I would look at Denver, in all likelihood. I'm not sleeping on Houston now that they've got VanVleet back."

"And I would also look at Minnesota because Ant-Man will be back by then. You know, you remember Ant-Man, right? Remember that superstar who averages 33 a game? Remember that superstar? You remember that? Remember who that dude is?"

"But it doesn't matter. He'll be back in a couple of months. It'll be good enough for them to get to the postseason, likely as a top-six seed. And as far as I'm concerned, again, the Lakers clearly are looking good right now."

"It's a testament to JJ Redick and his coaching staff and their ability to coach. It's a testament to Luka Doncic and his greatness. I feel it all. I get where you're coming from, but I'm not sold on the Lakers going far."

"I don't mind if they do because that means more time for me in Southern California. I ain't got no problems with it. I ain't rooting against them. I'm just telling you right now, I don't see it happening," he added when talking to a fan on the phone.

Near the end of the show, Smith took another phone call from a spectator who began defending the Lakers and what they're doing this season so far (10-2 record, six-game winning streak). Stephen A. Smith doubled down on his take.

"Luka Doncic is special. Right now, if we were to vote on a league MVP, he would win it. He's averaging 39.3 points a game. Thirty-nine a game. 39, eight, and eight on 49.8% shooting from the field and 40% shooting from three-point range. He has just been that dude."

"Okay, so I think the Lakers are going to be a good team. I think they have an exceptional young coach in JJ Redick and his coaching staff," Smith said in the beginning.

"The new ownership is led by Kushner and Bob Iger. Bob Iger happens to be, in my opinion, the Michael Jordan of sports. He's the greatest executive I've ever known, and he's a mentor and a friend. The bottom line is that I think the Lakers are in good hands, and the future is going to be incredibly bright," he added.

"But with that being said, I do not think they're getting past the second round. I'd be shocked if they did. I am on the record being controversial because I've never seen an NBA team with its top three players being white deliver a championship. It's never happened, and I'm here to tell you I don't think it's going to happen this year."

"The injuries to the Oklahoma City Thunder have not gone unnoticed. Denver is looking a bit worn down, even though Jokic and Murray still lead them. I mean, it's possible. I think Minnesota is a team to be reckoned with, with LaMelo Ball and Ant-Man. You can't ignore them, but Luka has given it to Minnesota in the postseason before, so who knows what the hell's going to happen with that?"

"The Lakers have a chance. I don't think it's going to materialize into a championship… No, I mean, listen, I don't care about it either. I'm just talking about logistics. I'm just talking about the actual facts," Stephen A. Smith explained.

"We've seen the Celtics with McHale and Bird, but you still had Dennis Johnson. You had Bill Russell before that, when you had Cousy and Havlicek and those guys. You could bring up the Lakers, but you still had Elgin Baylor, whether you had Jerry West or anybody else."

"You could bring up the Philadelphia 76ers, but you still had Wilt Chamberlain and ultimately Dr. J. You could bring up the Chicago Bulls. That speaks for itself. You could bring up the Pistons with Laimbeer, but that was Isiah's team."

"You could bring up the San Antonio Spurs, who were led by Duncan and Robinson. You could bring up the later Lakers with Shaq and Kobe. You could bring up the Boston Celtics with KG, Paul Pierce, and Ray Allen."

"You could bring up the Golden State Warriors with the Splash Brothers. You could bring up Cleveland with LeBron. You could bring up Golden State again with KD in the mix. You could bring up whoever the hell you want."

"There has never been, in my lifetime, an NBA team led by its top three players being white that delivered you a championship, when there was an abundance of brothers playing basketball. That hasn't happened, and I'm here to tell you it ain't going to happen. I can't see it coming," Stephen A. Smith said with a quick recap of the league's history.

"I understand that there are people who think otherwise and wish otherwise. The Olympics are coming to LA in 2028. Could you imagine, on the world stage, considering the global, iconic brand that the NBA is, if Luka Doncic somehow managed to win an NBA championship?"

"That would be huge for the league. It would be huge for the Olympics. It would be huge for LA. It would be huge for everything. But it ain't going to happen. I can't see it. Not a team with its top three players being white dudes. I'm sorry."

"I think that's controversial in some people's eyes. It ain't controversial in mine. I'm just telling you how it is. I'm calling it as I see it. I have never in my lifetime seen an NBA team with its top three players being white win a championship. It has never happened, and it ain't going to happen," Stephen A. Smith concluded .

Ultimately, Stephen A. Smith acknowledges the Lakers' impressive start but remains unconvinced they have the roster to win a championship. While Luka Doncic's MVP-level performances and JJ Redick's coaching have impressed him, he believes their shortcomings will become apparent in the playoffs.

With plenty of basketball left to play, the Lakers will have an opportunity to prove Smith wrong and silence their critics. It will be interesting to see if, for the first time in NBA history, a fully white team core wins an NBA championship this season.
